Suppose you have the small object 1 with velocity vector and mass:

v = (x, y, z)

Mass = m

And for large object 2 you have

V = (X, Y, Z)

mass = M

Then the relative velocity is

Vrel = V - v = (X, Y, Z) - (x, y, z) = (X-x, Y-y, Z-z)

The energy of the collision is :

E = (m) * |vrel|^2

E = (m) * (sqrt[(X-x)^2+(Y-y)^2+(Z-z)^2])^2

E= (m)*[(X-x)^2+(Y-y)^2+(Z-z)^2]

Make your damage proportional to that.

Your new velocity vector will be

momentum =(MV + mv)/(M+m)= [M (X,Y,Z) + m (x,y,z)]/(M+m)

=(MX+mx, MY+my, MZ+mz)/(M+m)

IMPORTANT: x,y,z etc are components of the velocity 3vector not the position coordinates.
